# Parse movie titles: take leading lines that are not blank and don't start with '-' and don't start with '#'
lines=[ln.strip() for ln in content.splitlines()]
titles=[]
for ln in lines:
    if not ln: 
        continue
    if ln.startswith('#'):
        continue
    if ln.startswith('-'):
        continue
    # Title lines in this note are simple and precede metadata bullets
    titles.append(ln)

# Remove any trailing metadata that accidentally got captured; keep only lines that look like titles (heuristic: no ':' and not starts with 'director')
cleaned=[]
for t in titles:
    if ':' in t:
        continue
    # metadata lines sometimes start with ' - ' in original; we already stripped '-' lines
    cleaned.append(t)

# The note uses title lines followed by bullets; ensure unique order but keep as-is
final_titles=[]
seen=set()
for t in cleaned:
    if t not in seen:
        final_titles.append(t)
        seen.add(t)

print('final_titles',len(final_titles),final_titles)
message=', '.join(final_titles)
print('message',message)

# Send text message
